definitions.explanation: Indicates the absence or non-existence of something. The negative counterpart of ある.
Indicates that someone doesn't possess something.

examples.english: I don't have time. / There is no time.

examples.japanese: お{金|かね}がないので、{買|か}えません。
examples.english: I can't buy it because I don't have money.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}はないですか。
examples.english: Are there no problems? / Is there no issue?

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{仕事|しごと}がないから、{家|いえ}でゆっくり{休|やす}みます。
examples.english: I don't have work today, so I'll relax at home.

notes: ない conjugates as an i-adjective: なくない (negative - 'is it not nonexistent?'), なくて (te-form), なかった (past). ない is the negative form of ある (to exist/have for inanimate things). For animate things (people/animals), the negative of いる is いない. The kanji 無い is sometimes used but hiragana is more common.
